transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Time: 10:00am PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Evan Park (Redwood CSM), Asha Patel (Quantaco Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Quantaco CTO), Diego Ramos (Quantaco SRE), Maya Chen (Quantaco Product)

Summary: Quick sync to go over the latest tokens/sec runs, look at caching assumptions in the cost model, and align on next benchmarks needed for a dedicated canary.
transcript_full:
00:00 Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining - quick roll call, looks like we have the usual crew. how's every- how's everything on your side, Asha?
00:12 Asha Patel: yeah hi thanks, we saw the draft cost sheet you sent, and we had a few questions on the cache assumptions. also Liam wanted to confirm the difference between hosted and dedicated numbers one more time, because our CFO keeps asking about $$ per token.
00:25 Jordan Lee: totally, that was the main intent today. priya's got the bench results, and we'll walk through the token/sec per dollar numbers and different batching/caching scenarios.
00:34 Priya Nambiar: yep, I ran two sets of runs last week - one on the hosted-like config (shared pool sim) and one on the dedicated config we reserved. quick note, the dedicated was on the T4-64-ish cluster variant - sorry that's internal shorthand, it's basically our reserved gpu mix for this POC.
00:52 Liam O'Connor: small correction, you said T4-64 - our infra folks wrote down A100-40 numbers, can you confirm which variant you actually used for the dedicated baseline?
01:02 Priya Nambiar: ah sorry, my bad, that was a shorthand; the dedicated runs used the a100-40 quantized path with int8 kernels. hosted sim was a mix of A100 and V100 emulation. there may be slight differences in kernel selection so numbers shouldn't be compared head-on without normalization.
01:17 Diego Ramos: ok noted. can you share the raw logs? we want to double-check tail latencies as well as aggregate tokens/sec.
01:23 Priya Nambiar: yep i've uploaded raw logs to the shared folder - link in the deck notes, file name is redwood_quantaco_bench_2026-07-13.tar.gz.
01:30 Asha Patel: perfect. can you run the 2k seq scenario again with our real prefix set? the earlier runs used synthetic prefixes and we think the cache hit rate will change.
01:42 Priya Nambiar: yes, that was on the list. i have a run queued for 2k and 4k seq with the sample prefixes from Diego. expected to finish by tomorrow.
01:50 Jordan Lee: great. ok let's look at the cost model slide - slide 5 in the deck. so baseline tokens/sec for dedicated at 2k seq right now is 7.8k tokens/sec per GPU, which with our reserved pricing translates to about 0.42 USD per 1k tokens in the naive config.
02:10 Maya Chen: wait - 0.42 per 1k seems higher than we expected. our spreadsheet had 0.27 per 1k for the hosted estimate. is that due to batch sizing?
02:20 Jordan Lee: good catch - hosted benefits from larger effective batching across multi-tenant pools and prefix cache reuse, so effective tokens/sec per dollar is better. but with dedicated you get predictability and lower p95, at the expense of raw cost unless you tune batching and caching.
02:36 Priya Nambiar: right, and that's where caching assumptions matter. the model has three cache-hit scenarios: low (5%), mid (25%), high (55%). at mid cache hit we saw roughly 18% cost reduction versus no cache because payloads skip early transformer layers with KV reuse.
02:51 Liam O'Connor: 55% high cache hit seems optimistic for us though - our prompts are fairly diverse. what's realistic given our prefix histogram?
02:58 Diego Ramos: our internal histogram shows ~12% exact prefix repeats, but if you include near-prefix reuse (same template but different IDs) maybe up to 22% after normalization. so mid is reachable with template normalization, but not high unless we do aggressive canonicalization.
03:15 Priya Nambiar: ok that maps. also batching trades off latency: we tested batch sizes 8, 16, 32. 16 was the sweet spot for p50/p95 vs throughput. at 32 you get ~25% more tokens/sec but p95 jumps ~120ms which breaches your SLOs.
03:33 Asha Patel: our SLO is p95 < 400ms for interactive assistant flows; can we hit that with batching 16 on dedicated?
03:40 Priya Nambiar: yes, 16 keeps p95 ~310-340ms depending on seq length and cache hits. if you enable prefix cache with mid hit rate, p95 tightens by ~30-40ms.
03:52 Jordan Lee: so practically, combination of batch=16 + mid cache hit gets you to about 0.34 USD per 1k tokens on dedicated, closer to hosted, with predictable latency.
04:04 Liam O'Connor: ok that's more palatable. can you explain where the tokens/sec/$ model accounts for KV cache memory costs and additional CPU overhead for cache lookups?
04:14 Priya Nambiar: yeah the model has a cache overhead line: we estimate 12% additional infra cost for cache memory and small CPU. that was folded into the dedicated reserved cost. that line is visible in the sheet - Jordan will share updated sheet with toggles.
04:27 Evan Park: just to add from CSM side, customers often get better cost at scale by combining smaller model variants for low-complexity queries - e.g., routing to a 4B for short intents and 30B for long contexts, that reduces average per-token cost. we can demo routing policy if you want.
04:44 Maya Chen: routing seems appealing, but we need to confirm quality thresholds. Asha, is A/B routing something you'd accept as long as quality is stable?
04:51 Asha Patel: yes, but we need baseline evals. for the POC success criteria, we said <10% quality regression for 20% cost savings. we'll formalize the metric.
05:02 Priya Nambiar: noted - I'll add routing/variant split into the next benchmark plan.
05:08 Diego Ramos: one operational question - if we enable bigger batching and caching, what's the recovery story on spikes? we have occasional traffic bursts and don't want tail latency chaos.
05:18 Jordan Lee: good question - Redwood has smart routing and autoscale policies; for dedicated pools we can set burst capacity and fallback to compatible hosted models for overflow. the canary should exercise spikes.
05:29 Priya Nambiar: also note batching introduces queueing latency - our measured queue wait at batch=32 under 2x QPS spike added ~180ms median before GPU. combined with model compute that was the issue for p95. so batching must be tuned with your SLO.
05:46 Liam O'Connor: can the runtime do dynamic batching that prioritizes latency-sensitive requests?
05:50 Priya Nambiar: yes, we have latency-priority queues; the runtime can shallow-batch priority traffic to keep p95 under threshold while still batching background work. there is a small throughput penalty but it helps.
06:02 Asha Patel: ok let's talk concrete numbers we need next week. Priya, you said you'll re-run 2k/4k with our prefixes - we need: tokens/sec, p50/p95, tokens/sec per dollar breakdown by batch sizes 8/16/32 and cache on/off. also include per-GPU and per-cluster extrapolations.
06:20 Priya Nambiar: got it. i'll push a run matrix and add raw logs.
06:24 Jordan Lee: Diego, for the traffic profile please send the p50/p95 seq lengths and percent repeated prefixes, that will let us model cacheable fraction.
06:33 Diego Ramos: will do, i'll export from our telemetry today and drop it in the shared folder.
06:38 Maya Chen: about quality, Asha will pick 200 prompts to evaluate across the small/large model routing. we'll need eval scripts - do you have an eval harness?
06:45 Priya Nambiar: yes we'll share the eval harness and example scoring rubric; we can run automated evals as part of the bench runs.
06:52 Asha Patel: perfect. on security/cost side, one more ask: can you show cost numbers with KMS-enabled private deployment? we may need Private later for compliance, but it affects unit economics.
07:03 Jordan Lee: yes KMS/HSM and private control plane add platform fee and some infra overhead. on the sheet there's a "private premium" toggle - default is +12% to unit cost. we'll produce a KMS-enabled scenario.
07:16 Liam O'Connor: final question - do you have a recommended canary rollout size for dedicated pool to validate cost and reliability without large spend?
07:24 Evan Park: typically customers do a 5-10% traffic canary on dedicated with automatic fallback. start small, monitor latency and error rates for 48 hours, then expand.
07:33 Jordan Lee: ok, we'll propose a canary plan in the follow-up email.
07:37 Priya Nambiar: action items summarized in the deck notes as well.
07:40 Asha Patel: thanks all. one quick note, the CFO will want the worst-case cost too - can you include no-cache, batch=8 worst-case in the sheet?
07:48 Jordan Lee: yep we'll include worst-case and best-case.
07:51 Maya Chen: ok that's it from product. thanks folks.
07:55 Jordan Lee: great, thanks everyone. we'll share the updated cost_econ_sheet.xlsx, the re-run results, and the canary plan. next sync same time next week unless we need to move. bye.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript had occasional word swaps (e.g., "Dedicate" instead of "Dedicated", "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cash"). we've retained minor errors to reflect natural transcription.

questions: What's the realistic cache hit rate given Quantaco's template diversity?
Can we keep p95 < 400ms while using batching for cost efficiency?
What's the recommended canary size and duration for dedicated pool testing?
